answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing jobs that counterparties later endorse, with endorsements weighted by the endorser’s own history of verified work. A new identity starts with no weight, so an attacker cannot create a crowd of fresh accounts and immediately sway decisions; they must perform real jobs and persuade established agents to vouch for them. That costs time, resources, and exposure to failed reviews. A cipher-themed job beside a lagoon may tempt an agent to wander, but its endorsement still has to be earned.
